title: the no-hand-drop tooth asks what a leak is made of, not what it says
intention: db_domain's no-hand-drop tooth reds a proof that drops a table or mints a nonce by hand, and never a proof that only mentions those words in a string.
why: Measured 2026-11-12: test_no_proof_drops_a_table_by_hand (201a37bf1613 clause 4) is a text scan, and it redded test_an_owned_index_is_owner_gated.py for an SQL-injection payload, a string handed to store.add_owned_index. A mention became a catch, and it cost a proof-only repair to d494ff4ae955.
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: the tooth must measure the leak, not the words; a false red is distrust spent where none was owed.
how: Replace the text scan with a module-level AST predicate _hand_leaks(src) -> list[str] in test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process.py (address_rule.py's pattern): a Call to .execute/.executemany whose first argument holds a str Constant matching DROP TABLE, and an Assign/AnnAssign to the Name _NONCE; a SyntaxError is an offender. The tooth runs it over cairn/**/proofs/*.py. A new proof, test_a_mention_is_not_a_hand_drop.py, imports the predicate and holds one tooth per clause over fixture sources plus the corpus.

clauses.claim: a fixture source that mentions DROP TABLE only inside a string handed to a non-execute call yields no offence
a fixture with cur.execute(f"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {t}") yields an offence naming its line
a fixture with _NONCE = os.getpid() yields an offence naming its line
the whole cairn/**/proofs/*.py corpus yields no offence under the predicate

decisions.text: D1: _LEAK_SPELLINGS and the text scan give way to the AST predicate _hand_leaks in the existing proof; test_no_proof_drops_a_table_by_hand calls it.
D2: the new proof holds one tooth per clause over fixture sources and the corpus, PROVES keys 1..4.

measured.saw: text scan hit 1 proof (an injection payload, a mention); the AST predicate hit 0 proofs and caught both leak shapes in fixtures

verdicts.discriminating_observation: Clause 1 can fail: the text grep this replaced reds the fixture that mentions DROP TABLE in an add_owned_index payload. Clauses 2 and 3 can fail: a predicate that catches nothing, or the wrong line, misses the exact ['... @ 2', '... @ 3'] lists. Clause 4 can fail: any proof that executes a DROP TABLE or assigns _NONCE reds it. Hollow measured: reverting the tooth to the pre-build commit reds all four teeth.
